newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cable & Wireless to make Singapore statement.
newsitem.headline: Cable & Wireless to make Singapore statement.

text.p: British telecommunications company Cable & Wireless (C&W) is likely to make an announcement shortly on its plans for the Singapore terrestrial telephone market, a senior CW executive said on Thursday.

Ross Cormack, C&W's Asian regional director for mobile phone services, said the company would say then how it intended to bid for a licence to operate basic telecommunications services in the island from 2000.
"I am sure that an announcement will be made shortly but I cant say any further at this time," Cormack told Reuters.

C&W's Southeast Asia and Pacific chief executive, Richard Goswell, told Reuters in December the company would definitely make a bid for the licence but had not yet decided which local partners to link up with.
Foreign companies are allowed to hold up to 49 percent of any consortium bidding for a licence.

Singapore has said it will allow one or two more companies or consortiums to compete directly with the current domestic monopoly, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd, operating land-based local and international telephone networks from April 1, 2000.
Analysts have suggested C&W is likely to announce it is linking up with two local partners, Keppel Telecommunications and Transportation and the local newspaper monopoly, Singapore Press Holdings.
Both these companies have said they will make a bid with undisclosed partners.
There may also be another foreign partner involved in the consortium, they say.
Cormack declined to give any hint of the content of the expected announcement by C&W.
Two other groups have also said they bid for the licence. These groups include British Telecommunications Plc and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.
